newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU expects Lyonnais plan Friday, decision in Nov.
newsitem.headline: EU expects Lyonnais plan Friday, decision in Nov.

text.p: France is expected to submit a new restructuring plan for Credit Lyonnais to the European Commission tomorrow at the latest, a Commission source said on Thursday, adding that an EU decision would not be ready before November.

The plan is expected to contain a commitment by France's new socialist government to privatise the bank, as planned under a previous rescue plan. But it is unclear whether the bank will receive a new cash injection to boost its solvency ratio.
The Commission in 1995 cleared 45 billion francs ($7.27 billion) in French subsidies for the bank which nearly collapsed due to an ill-fated expansion spree in the 90s.
The conditions imposed by the Commission proved too tough, however, causing the payment of 3.9 billion francs in emergency aid in September 1996 while waiting for a revised restructuring plan.

The French government at the end of last year estimated the additional measures at between eight billion to 10 billion francs. But some analysts do not expect a further recapitalisation as the bank is recovering quicker than expected.
Bank chairman Jean Peyrelevade was recently quoted as saying the bank would need less than five billion francs in extra funds to ready it for privatisation.

Part of the new plan will consist in neutralising the cost of financing a loan of 135 billion francs granted below market rates to finance the spinoff of the bank's bad assets to a separate holding company.
The Commission source said the new plan would immediately be sent to Lehman Brothers which has been advising the EU on the case. $ = 6.19 francs
